known_gaps: Brief A vs Brief B – `brief-ab.md` contains both. Brief A says it never uses `add_note`, and Brief B requires it for products without a promise. I built the Brief B superset, so a one-product Brief A call will still call `add_note`. If the call is scored under Brief A, that is a mismatch.

failed `transfer_to_agent` – the brief gives no path for this. The agent tells the customer plainly that the transfer failed, then closes with the outcome the request would have had (e.g. `transferred` / `restructuring`). Under the brief's table this records a transfer that did not happen.
persuasion-attempt and per-product tallies are kept by the model from the prompt; no code enforces them.

`maxRetries` is 1 on the write tools (`create_promise`, `schedule_callback`, `transfer_to_agent`, `add_note`, `close_call`). It is untested whether the platform retries an `ok:false` reply that comes back as HTTP 200.
coverage not fully assessed: the fallback path reports only the gaps its agent noticed
